subject: Re: Availability commitment and monthly credit structure - SkyTech
messages:

Cc: SkyTech Procurement <procurement@skytech.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Availability commitments for Enterprise deployment

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough on Friday. We ran this up the chain and procurement asked us to confirm the availability guarantees you are willing to put in the enterprise contract for our private deployment. Our standard requirement for customer-facing production services is 99.99% monthly uptime for core API endpoints and explicit latency guidance for tail latencies (p95 and p99) for small/medium payloads.

Two narrow asks from their side:
- Can Redwood commit to 99.99% monthly uptime for the dedicated Private cluster (single-region)?
- If not, can you provide a transparent monthly credit schedule tied to downtime minutes and an explicit exclusion list (maintenance windows, force majeure, planned patch windows)?

Procurement is also asking for a clause that limits scheduled maintenance to no more than 4 hours per month and requires 72-hour notice. Finally, they want the baseline p95 latency for 256-token requests to be under 200ms, p99 under 700ms; outages that impact latency SLAs should be eligible for credits too.

Can you share a redline or proposal this week so we can move to legal review?

Best,
Katherine Reynolds
Head of Platform Operations
SkyTech

Katherine —

Appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: our standard enterprise SLA for Private deployments today is 99.9% monthly uptime. We typically offer tighter commitments (99.95% or 99.99%) on reserved Dedicated pools with a stronger pricing/commitment profile.

Proposal to accelerate review without blocking your legal:
- Offer a 99.95% uptime SLO for the first 12 months for this deployment, with an automatic review at month 9 tied to observed telemetry and usage.
- Monthly service credit schedule (draft):
  - >= 99.95% and < 100%: no credit
  - 99.0% to <99.95%: 10% of monthly subscription fee
  - 95.0% to <99.0%: 30% credit
  - <95.0%: 60% credit or negotiation of termination rights
- Scheduled maintenance: standard window 2 hours/month with 72-hour notice; we can extend to 4 hours/month with exception review and a committed maintenance blackout for scheduled product launches.
- Latency: we can commit to p95 < 200ms for 256-token inference in normal load, p99 target 700ms but this will be a best-effort target tied to request distribution and model choice. If you need strict latency credits, we should pin the model family and throughput profile (this affects kernel selection and capacity planning).

I've attached a redline (SLA-Redline-v3.pdf) and a simple monthly-credits-matrix.xlsx showing how credits would accrue. If we can get a go-ahead on 99.95% initial commitment, Jordan and I will route a limited exception through ops and legal.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call to finalize.

—Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Availability commitments for Enterprise deployment

Dropping in with an ops/legal perspective. Key considerations before we accept 99.95 for Private:

1) Capacity provisioning: Private clusters for SkyTech will be isolated; to guarantee 99.95 we need a dedicated hot spare node per shard and an accelerated replacement SLA for failed GPUs. That increases cost materially — call out to sales when you compute pricing.

2) Maintenance windows: 4 hrs/month is aggressive for major infra changes. We should keep standard 2 hrs/month, allow up to 8 hrs/quarter for larger migrations with preapproved blackout dates. Also require emergency patch exceptions for critical security CVEs.

3) Credit cap: propose a cap at 60% monthly credit and a maximum monetary cap equal to 2x of monthly committed fees — prevents outsized exposure.

4) Latency as an SLA is tricky: p99 is workload-dependent. If the customer wants p99 credits, we must define request size buckets, model pinning, and a traffic profile and possibly add a per-query SLi (service level indicator) instrumentation to compute credits. That tooling will delay signoff by ~3 weeks.

Recommend we offer 99.95 with the following guardrails in the contract redline: dedicated capacity sizing, spare-node requirement, credit cap, pinned model families for latency credits, and a defined instrumentation plan. Jordan — can you draft a one-page price delta for the added infra (hot spare, replacement SLA)?

-Vivek
VP, Product Operations

Marissa, Jordan, Vivek —

Thank you — this is helpful and pragmatic. Procurement reviewed the redline and the credit cap is acceptable, provided the 2x monthly fee monetary cap is explicitly called out (they want a formula clause). They also accepted the 99.95% starting point with a contractual review at month 9.

Two final asks before we request our GC to sign:

- Provide the one-page price delta for the dedicated hot-spare and accelerated replacement SLA. Procurement wants it bundled as a monthly addendum item rather than a one-time fee.

If you can provide the price delta and the small wording tweak, we'll open a GC review and aim to sign the SLA schedule next week.

Katherine
